title: Receive signed webhooks of the payments provider

pr.title: Add the payments webhook
pr.description:
Adds `POST /hooks/payments`. It checks the `X-Payments-Signature` header with the parser of the previous PR, refuses deliveries signed more than 5 minutes off, stores each new event of a handled type, and queues the `webhook-event` job. Duplicates and other event types answer 200, so the provider stops retrying.

New setting: `PAYMENTS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. docs/webhooks.md describes the route and its answers.

traps.why: timingSafeEqual throws on buffers of different length, but the unchanged parseSignatureHeader() keeps only v1 values of exactly 64 lowercase hex characters, so each buffer is 32 bytes like the HMAC-SHA256 digest.

The header and docs/webhooks.md give t in seconds and the clock is in milliseconds, which looks like a unit mismatch, but the unchanged parseSignatureHeader() returns t in milliseconds and keeps the sent value as timestamp for the signed payload.

JSON.parse can throw, but the body has a valid signature at this point, and the unchanged withErrors() wrapper that main.ts puts around the router turns a SyntaxError into a 400 answer. A test checks the SyntaxError.

has() and then add() look like a check-then-act race that queues a duplicate twice, but the unchanged EventStore.add() inserts the event and its job in one statement with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so a racing duplicate inserts nothing and gets 200.
